issue.title: sase repo open plans fails applying commit b10820e6: non-bead conflict in split_patch_handler.md
issue.description: 'sase repo open plans' fails applying commit b10820e6 ("Add SDD files for split_patch_handler") with a non-bead conflict in 202608/split_patch_handler.md, though the worktree is clean afterwards. Proposed by sase-js.9 (Adoption, glossary, and documentation) during landing of epic sase-js (Artifact reference contract). Reproduction: 'sase repo open plans' in workspace 14 hit the rebase/apply conflict on that commit; the plans worktree is clean after the failed attempt.

payload.close_reason: Backlog cut to seven (owner-requested, 2026-08-12): single unreproduced report with no standing impact. The bead's own reproduction notes that the plans worktree is clean after the failed apply of b10820e6, so 'sase repo open plans' recovers rather than leaving a broken sidecar, and no agent has reported being blocked by it since (no +1 in 6+ hours of heavy plan-sidecar traffic). Filed as a drive-by observation by sase-js.9 during epic landing, not root-caused. A one-off rebase conflict on a single historical commit does not justify a large task ahead of the currently-red gates. Reopen with a +1 if it recurs or if it ever leaves the plans worktree unusable.

evidence.note: Independent post-close reproduction on 2026-08-13 at HEAD 7e4ac6d7c while reviewing active epic sase-ku before implementing monitor_wait_resolution.md: 'sase repo open plans -r ...' failed rebasing commit 126149cd (Add SDD files for document_ref_expansion_format) with an add/add conflict in 202608/document_ref_expansion_format.md and LEFT the plans sidecar at detached HEAD mid-rebase (AA conflict markers). The standing conflict then made just check fail plan-links validation on invalid YAML frontmatter until I ran git rebase --abort, which restored main clean (ahead 4, behind 5). This exactly contradicts the close reason's assumption that repo open recovers cleanly and demonstrates standing impact on unrelated verification.

Independent recurrence during monitor_starter_row_misclassified monitor handoff on 2026-08-13: running 'sase repo open sase-core -r ...' first attempted to pull the workspace SDD/plans clone and failed rebasing commit 4d59e7a9 ('Add SDD files for monitor_starter_row_misclassified') with a non-bead conflict in 202608/monitor_starter_row_misclassified.md. The command printed the failed rebase diagnostic, then 'Cleaning workspace... Updating workspace to origin/master... Workspace ready' and returned the linked sase-core path, so this instance recovered cleanly rather than leaving the sidecar stuck. It still confirms the same root class tracked here: repo-open's plans sidecar refresh can trip add/add/non-bead conflicts on recently authored plan files in unrelated workflows.

payload.entry: Triage sweep 2026-08-14 (requested by the project owner: keep the seven highest-impact open tasks, close the rest; master 443566f7d, workspace sase_13). Verified still live in-tree, and closed on priority rather than on staleness: sase-je (src/sase/ace/restore.py:220 still passes base_name positionally while 'sase stitch create --help' shows only [-n NAME], so sase restore still fails end to end -- cheap, well-scoped fix if you want it back) and sase-ca (sase memory read generated_skills.md still carries the 'Commit Skills per Runtime' table asserting /sase_hg_commit is Gemini-only, contradicting Tier-1 Uniform Agent Runtimes; editing a memory note needs explicit owner approval anyway, so this cannot be worked unattended). Closed as low-reach: sase-jv, sase-l5 (repo resolution from a numbered workspace), sase-kb (one commit's rebase conflict in the plans repo, worktree clean afterwards), sase-l0 (memory init --no-commit blast radius), sase-lq (Grok Build double-loads AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md -- duplicate instructions, not wrong ones), sase-lp (a ~2h one-shot migration that has already been run). sase-ks is additionally superseded in substance: commit 9df15dbe2 made LaunchSelection the single consuming boundary for pooled aliases and reconciles root agent_meta.json, prompt_step_*.json, and chat metadata against the model actually invoked. Re-file any of these with a +1 if it bites during real work.
